body:
Post-merge readiness rerun against master `3a83b2c65b76a89e3d47c33acd0cf5ddbe48df3b` (6 October 2026, macOS 26.4.1 arm64) still reproduces this issue after #6225.

Fresh projects in FileProvider-backed Documents were initialized and built for all nine bundled templates (`ios`, `react`, `react-js`, `svelte`, `svelte-js`, `vanilla`, `vanilla-js`, `vue`, `vue-js`). Each was packaged twice with the freshly built CLI. All package commands returned 0, but **all nine bundles failed delayed `codesign --verify --deep --strict`** with `resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed`. Seven initially verified successfully before asynchronous metadata returned. The generated `bin` directories remained real directories and `.wails-provider-checked` cached their path as local. Bundle attributes later included `com.apple.FinderInfo` and `com.apple.fileprovider.fpfs#P`.

A fresh vanilla `wails3 dev` also failed signing before launch in Documents. Developer ID signing of the affected React bundle failed strict verification. In unsynced `/private/tmp` controls, dev restart verification, universal arm64+x86_64 packaging, and Developer ID signing all passed.

The current helper checks a newly created empty `.app` probe after 2.5 seconds, then permanently caches a negative detection result. The observations are consistent with a false negative when FileProvider metadata arrives later. A successful immediate codesign check does not establish a durable signature.

Reproduction:
1. Compile the CLI from the above master.
2. Initialize a fresh template beneath FileProvider-backed Documents; build against that checkout.
3. Run `wails3 build`, then `wails3 package` twice.
4. Check whether `bin` was relocated, and inspect `.wails-provider-checked`.
5. Repeat strict codesign verification after provider metadata has arrived (including a substantially longer wait than the current 2.5-second probe).
6. Repeat with `wails3 dev` and Developer ID signing.

Acceptance criteria: a fresh project and repeated package/dev builds must avoid a permanently cached false-local result, and signatures must remain valid after asynchronous provider processing. Keep this in the GA milestone; the post-merge result is a release blocker on affected Macs.
